newsitem.title: USA: SIMSCI, Shell in software pact.
newsitem.headline: SIMSCI, Shell in software pact.

text.p: Simulation Sciences Inc. (SIMSCI) Thursday announced it paid $1.5 million to acquire Shell Oil Co software as part of a pact to jointly develop computer programs for industrial plants.
Under terms of the agreement, SIMSCI will acquire PROFIT, Shell Oil's business planning software, for the one-time payment.
SIMSCI will also make an initial $1 million payment for certain exclusive worldwide marketing rights and the right to purchase other Shell software.
By combining the companies' software, Shell hopes to improve the efficiency of its industrial operations, including crude oil refineries the company said.

"We are convinced that combining Shell's innovative planning and advanced process control technology with SIMSCI's ...technology will increase our... operating efficiencies," said Paul Cuneo of Shell Oil Products Co.
Based in Houston, Shell Oil Product Co. is a subsidiary of Shell Oil Co, which owns seven U.S oil refineries.

SIMSCI Inc. provides simulation software and related services to the petroleum, petrochemical and industrial chemical industries as well as the engineering and construction firms that support those industries.
